Required-field completeness is enforced per request: every applicable custom field that is required on creation (or required on completion, once the entity is completed) must be included in the request unless it already holds a stored value; the 400 error lists the missing fields by id and name. Validation is atomic: if any submitted field fails validation (unknown template, invalid option, exceeding the template's configured max length, missing required value, or no existing field row), the entire request fails with a 400 and no values are written. An archived template stays updatable while the record still carries a live value row for it — whether a field is available on a record is decided by the record's own value row, not the template's archived flag. For the TASKS and TASK_ASSETS zones the set of available templates depends on the site setting "Use individual Custom Fields for each Business Unit": when it is enabled, only templates belonging to the task's business unit are accepted; a template from another business unit is rejected as not available for the record. Business-unit access is enforced on writes for BU-scoped zones (TASKS, TASK_ASSETS, WORK_ORDERS, PROJECTS, PURCHASE_ORDERS) — updating a record owned by a business unit the caller cannot access is refused. For TASK_ASSETS, custom fields are not available while the parent task is in the Quote status.

ops.d:
Deletes a calendar schedule record: a task schedule, an ad-hoc event schedule, or a periodic occurrence.

Any schedule returned by `GET /schedules` or `POST /schedules` can be deleted. Two kinds of record are
refused with `422`: a periodic template's baseline schedules, which define the template rather than an
occurrence, and schedule records with no user, asset or crew resource attached. Timesheet entries are not
schedules and return `404`.

- `USER` and `ASSET` schedules: the single schedule record identified by `scheduleId` is deleted. For an
  ad-hoc event with several resources this removes only the targeted resource; the event's other schedules
  are untouched.
- Crew schedules: `POST /schedules` with a `CREW` resource creates one schedule record per crew member and
  returns each as its own `USER` or `ASSET` item. Deleting any one of those records removes the **whole crew
  occurrence** (every member record for that crew, task or event, and start date), mirroring the office
  calendar's "remove crew" action. `X-Affected-Count` reports how many records were removed.
- Periodic occurrences: deleting the last remaining occurrence of a periodic template regenerates the
  template's next occurrence from its baseline at the template's due date, exactly as the office calendar
  does.

Deleting a schedule replicates the data side-effects of removing it from the calendar: removal of queued
reminders (when no other resource remains in the schedule group), Google Calendar removal for synced users,
geofence clean-up, and periodic regeneration. No event message or cancellation email is sent: the
schedule-deleted event message the office calendar triggers is not sent for API deletes.

**Optional query parameters:**
- `businessUnitId`: Override the business unit whose timezone and calendar-sync settings the delete side-effects run under (defaults to the business unit the schedule belongs to).

**Permissions required:**
- `Scheduling` delete permission.
- `Scheduling` delete field permission on Tasks.
- Access to the business unit the schedule belongs to (the caller's own business unit, or one granted through
  the Business Unit access settings). Otherwise `403`.
- Client users are not permitted to access this endpoint.

Requires "Work Orders" edit permission.

Inbound work orders are not supported — the request will be rejected with a 400 error.
